title: Finite-fibre base open for a closed subset in a proper algebraic space
statement: Algebraic spaces and their etale scheme charts are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if its diagonal is a closed immersion, it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts, and its underlying map is closed after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Fibre products and geometric fibres use [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to S$ be proper, and let $T\subseteq|X|$ be a closed subset. For a field-valued point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, let $T_{\bar s}$ be the inverse image of $T$ in $|X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega|$. The set of points $s\in S$ for which $T_{\bar s}$ is finite for an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$ is an open subset $V_{f,T}\subseteq S$. For every scheme morphism $g:S^\prime\to S$, let $f^\prime:X^\prime=X\times_SS^\prime\to S^\prime$ and let $T^\prime$ be the inverse image of $T$ in $|X^\prime|$. Then $V_{f^\prime,T^\prime}=g^{-1}(V_{f,T})$. At a field-valued point over $s$, finiteness of $T_{\bar s}$ is equivalent to finiteness after any field extension of $\kappa(s)$, including $\kappa(s)$ itself. Empty subsets and empty fibres are allowed. No flatness, local finite presentation, Noetherian-base, or dimension assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 0A4Y (lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood), closed-subset consequence using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03IQ (lemma-reduced-closed-subspace), and decent-spaces.tex Tag 0ACK (lemma-conditions-on-fibre-and-qf).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] to $T\subseteq|X|$, obtaining a reduced closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with support $T$. Set $h=f\circ i:Z\to S$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper] the closed immersion $i$ is proper, so [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition] applied to $i$ and the proper map $f$ shows that $h$ is proper, hence separated, quasi-compact and locally of finite type. In particular it satisfies the separated finite-type hypotheses of the fibre criterion.

By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the sheaf fibre products $X_K$ and $Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ are algebraic spaces with the categorical fibre-product universal property. For a point $s\in S$ and any field extension $K/\kappa(s)$, [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] applied to $X_K\to X$ identifies $|Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K|$ with the inverse image $T_K$ of $T$ in $|X_K|$. By [lem-sfb-space-finite-fibre-quasifinite-criterion] applied to $h$, this set is finite if and only if $h$ is quasi-finite at every point of $|Z|$ above $s$. In particular this characterizes the condition in the item when $K$ is an algebraic closure.

By [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open], the quasi-finite locus $U=Q_h$ is open in $|Z|$. Let $C=|Z|\setminus U$. Properness of $h$, obtained in Step 1 from [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper] and [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition], implies that its point map is closed, so $h(C)$ is closed in $S$. Thus $V=S\setminus h(C)$ is open. A point $s$ belongs to $V$ precisely when there is no non-quasi-finite point of $h$ over $s$, equivalently when $h$ is quasi-finite at every point over $s$.

source.place: Tag 0A4Y (lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood), proof, construction of the complement of the closed image.

proof.text: The equivalence of Step 2 and the description in Step 3 give $s\in V$ if and only if $T_{\bar s}$ is finite, for each $s\in S$. Consequently $V=V_{f,T}$, proving openness. If the fibre is empty, the condition that all its points lie in $U$ is vacuous, so this argument includes empty fibres and the case $T=\varnothing$.

The criterion in Step 2 is independent of the chosen extension $K/\kappa(s)$: [lem-sfb-space-finite-fibre-quasifinite-criterion] always gives the same condition on the points of $Z$ over $s$. The support identification of [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] therefore proves equivalence of finiteness of $T_K$ for all these fields. This proves the field-valued clause, including the original residue field itself; it does not assert equality of the numbers of geometric and ordinary points.

Let $g:S^{\prime}\to S$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] over $B=S$ with $Y=S$ and $Y'=S^{\prime}$: the given $f$ is proper and $g$ is an arbitrary morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$, so $f^{\prime}:X\times_SS^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ is proper. The pullback of the closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow X$ has support $T^{\prime}$ by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], and $T^{\prime}$ is closed. Thus the openness argument already proved applies to $(f^{\prime},T^{\prime})$. For $s^{\prime}\in S^{\prime}$ put $s=g(s^{\prime})$ and choose an algebraic closure $L$ of $\kappa(s^{\prime})$. The field maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s^{\prime})\to L$ exhibit $L$ also as an extension of $\kappa(s)$. The algebraic-space fibre-product universal property in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $X^{\prime}\times_{S^{\prime}}\operatorname{Spec}L$ with $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}L$: maps into either side are exactly a map into $X$ and a map into $\operatorname{Spec}L$ agreeing in $S$. Under this identification, the inverse image of $T^{\prime}$ is the inverse image $T_L$ of $T$. By the field independence of Step 5 (using [lem-sfb-space-finite-fibre-quasifinite-criterion]), this is finite exactly when $s\in V_{f,T}$. Hence $s^{\prime}\in V_{f^{\prime},T^{\prime}}$ if and only if $g(s^{\prime})\in V_{f,T}$, giving the required equality of open subsets. No claim that reduced induced structures commute with base change is used.

lean.statement: theorem isOpen_closedSupportFiniteFibreLocus {B : Scheme.{u}} (S : Over B) (X : AlgebraicSpace B) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace S) (hf : MapIsProper f) (T : Set (Point X.obj.obj)) (hT : IsClosed T) : IsOpen (closedSupportFiniteFibreLocus f.hom.hom T) ∧ (∀ (S' : Over B) (g : S' ⟶ S), closedSupportFiniteFibreLocus (Limits.pullback.snd f.hom.hom (yoneda.map g)) (closedSupportFibre f.hom.hom T g) = g.left ⁻¹' closedSupportFiniteFibreLocus f.hom.hom T) ∧ ∀ (s : S.left) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (S.left.residueField s) K], s ∈ closedSupportFiniteFibreLocus f.hom.hom T ↔ (closedSupportFibre f.hom.hom T (supportResidueFieldPoint S s K)).Finite
